record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Must the ratio λₙ₊₂/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding ratio for the n-ball, namely j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}² with p = (n−2)/2?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ show that λₙ₊₂/λ₁ ≤ (λₙ₊₂/λ₁)|n-ball = j²_{p+2,1}/j²_{p,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain. Consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose spectrum consists of an increasing sequence $0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) \le \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$ of eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity). For an $n$-ball $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the eigenvalues are explicitly given in terms of zeros of Bessel functions: setting $p = (n-2)/2$ and letting $j_{\nu,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$, one has $\lambda_1(B) = j_{p,1}^2/R^2$ and $\lambda_{n+2}(B) = j_{p+2,1}^2/R^2$, where $R$ is the radius of $B$. In particular, the ratio $\lambda_{n+2}(B)/\lambda_1(B) = j_{p+2,1}^2/j_{p,1}^2$ is scale-invariant.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{n+2}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{j_{p+2,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2},$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is (up to a set of measure zero) a ball.
artifact.status_search_result: This is part of the family of Ashbaugh–Benguria higher-order eigenvalue ratio conjectures. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:1810.09415 and subsequent papers on the PPW conjecture for higher eigenvalues) makes partial progress toward such isoperimetric bounds but does not establish the sharp bound $\lambda_{n+2}/\lambda_1 \le j_{p+2,1}^2/j_{p,1}^2$ for arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Ashbaugh-Benguria's Conjecture about Lower Order Dirichlet Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Makes an important step toward the proof of a conjecture by Ashbaugh-Benguria, strengthening the known inequality on the ratio of the first two Dirichlet eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward, but not full resolution of, the higher-order Ashbaugh–Benguria ratio conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On the PPW Conjecture for Hopf-Symmetric Sets in Non-compact Rank One Symmetric Space
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work addressing extensions of the PPW-type conjectures, indicating the broader family of conjectures is still actively studied.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture and its extensions remain an active research topic.
